Brazil’s presidential election has delivered a dramatic comeback for 81-year-old Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who overturned a 2.2-million-vote deficit in the first round to defeat Bolsonaro Jr, in the runoff.
In episode 1925 of , ThePrint Editor-in-Chief Shekhar Gupta looks at the factors that helped Lula, & the challenges that lie ahead for him. It also examines how this could be a setback for Trump, who backed Bolsonaro Jr as part of his push to shift Latin America to the right, & the significance of this win for India-Brazil ties.
